title: Benchmarking Analog and Ensemble‐Based Seasonal Forecasting Strategies for Water Management in the Upper Rio Grande Basin
content:
ABSTRACT

In the southwestern US, declining runoff efficiencies driven by a warming climate may be undermining water supply forecast (WSF) methods used for reservoir management, and particularly those that rely on linear statistical methods and historical analog techniques. In some regions, seasonal water allocations use inflow sequences derived from matching historical streamflow analogs (“traces”) to statistical WSF seasonal volumes, even as model-based ensemble forecasting expands. We evaluate whether ensemble forecasts can provide an improved source of sequences (versus analogs) via a hindcast-based benchmarking assessment, applying process-based hydrologic modeling for US Bureau of Reclamation inflow points in the Upper Rio Grande (URG) basin. We demonstrate the viability of model-based prediction for guiding reservoir planning compared to existing analog-based practices, using the Ensemble Streamflow Prediction (ESP) technique to develop 49 years of April 1 hindcasts. Across thirteen URG forecast points, the post-processed ESP mean sequences improved hydrograph shape relative to analog-based sequences, with a median Kling-Gupta Efficiency (KGE) increase of +0.09. For peak flow characteristics, performance was comparable. These results support ESP-based inflow sequences as a practical alternative to analog methods, and demonstrate an early implementation of the SUMMA-mizuRoute watershed modeling framework for regional water modeling and seasonal ensemble streamflow forecasting.
